evidence_selected.sentence: There is no precise definition of surrounding base, but Denali,[2] Mount Kilimanjaro[3] and Nanga Parbat[4] are possible candidates for the tallest mountain on land by this measure.
Mount  Everest, located in Nepal and Tibet, is usually said to be the highest mountain  on Earth.
Everest has a height of 8,848 m and is considered to be the tallest mountain on Earth.
Everest owes its popularity to the impressive title of 'highest mountain in the world', but in reality, it isn't - not according to science.
Mount Everest is the world's tallest mountain above sea level.

If you really want to bicker about what constitutes the "highest point," consider this: The summit of Ecuador's Mount Chimborazo is 6,800 feet (2,072 m) farther from the center of the Earth than Everest's peak, although Chimborazo only rises 20,564 feet (6,268 m) above sea level.

Mount Everest is part of the Himalayan mountain range, situated on the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
